route.geometry: take the right flagpole to the long planter below (G1 p069); lines you up for the car jump
ride along the right wall 'above and before the hazard' (G1 p074); LP1 8:50-8:52
ramp over the car, or avoid it but keep a good line (G1 p074; PS12)

route.from: walkway end jump (or the end of the walkway's left-edge rail, G1 'really daring', LP1 8:52-8:53)
route.geometry: blind launch on a line that crosses the two rods; LP1 passes through the 200 icon ('50 50 GRIND + BONUS 200')
land in a grind ≈ 5-8 m above the water floor (LP1 8:54)
≈ 30-40 m descending grind, 'a long haul' (G1 p074); LP1 ≈ 4 s
ollie between them at just the right moment to collect the tape (G1 p074); LP1 8:57 timer 1:15
or give the rails below a quick grind (G1 p074)

skillGates: commit to a blind launch with a pre-planned line
land a grind on a thin elevated rail
timed hop between parallel rails (G1 p068)
collectibles.failure: a miss drops to the water-hazard floor past the launch on a one-way course; retry via the escalators and back round ≈ 15-25 s, or a skilled jump from below (TAS); missing the hop at the end loses the attempt
collectibles.timeFromSpawnS: LP1 45 (timer 2:00→1:15, LP1 8:57, with S, directories 1-2, K, fountain on the way); launch-to-tape ≈ 5 (8:52-8:57); TAS1 ≈ 18 (timer 2:00→1:42, TAS1 1:52); LP12 timer 0:49 in a later run (0:11:47)
collectibles.why: Tests the grind skills taught by the first two levels on the level's signature object (Tony's favourite spot); it hangs over A so every player sees it, but the approach must be chosen a section earlier

guidance: The rods hang over the water hazard and the A rail, where every route rejoins, so everyone sees them from below; the tape glints at their far end
The launch hides the rods: G1 says you launch 'almost blindly'; the level relies on the player having seen them from below
The approach is chosen a section earlier (right flagpole at the first escalator, or the second balcony)
A 200 icon in the launch air and a 100 beside the tape confirm the line once on it
Directories stand across the main route as waypoints in course order
Hidden on purpose: the walkway launch towards the rods and the second-balcony leap
designLogic: Visible from below, reached from above: the tape is over the A rail but reachable only from the walkway or balconies
The tape uses the level's star feature, the hanging rods (Tony's favourite spot); hopping between them is the skill (G1 p068)
A linear level makes the choice early: the approach is decided a section before the rods
Blind launch, readable landing: long paired rods give a wide landing window; the difficulty is commitment
Precision at the end: the tape sits between the rods at the far end and needs a timed hop
Failure is expensive on a one-way course (≈ 15-25 s to climb back), after two levels of cheap failure
Three graded approaches (walkway and car, walkway rail, second balcony) plus the TAS Flying Leap from below
In a linear level the letter tour equals the course
Directories are gates in course order; the last blocks the exit
The level falls about three storeys, so the tape route needs no pumping
Progression over the first three tapes: one jump from spawn (1) → roof, pipe and canopy (2) → blind launch, long suspended grind, timed hop, costly miss (3)
THPS 1+2 rewards the neighbourhood: Across The Light Beam and the Flying Leap goal let near-misses score
remakeChanges: Tape unchanged (suspended light rails above the water; right-side car ramp approach per PS12)
Adds lower beams below the light rails with Across The Light Beam (250)
Goal objects: directories plus 5 toy robots; named-gap goals Coffee Grind (nosegrind) and Flying Leap (airwalk)
Letters in the same course order
Gaps: Going Up/Down not listed; new Exit Stage Right/Left, The Long Rail, The Short Rail
transfer: Hanging-rod crystal: two parallel static rods on cables over water or a pit, ≈ 30-40 m long, falling ≈ 2-4 m; crystal between them at the far end so the skater must ollie across (a grind ollie pops ≈ 2.4 m, enough for a ≈ 1.5-2 m sideways hop)

Launch from an elevated side walkway ending in a kicker aimed along the rods; a pickup in the launch air confirms the line; rely on the 2.1 m grind snap at the rods' near end for a slightly blind launch
Route the main line under the rods (a low rail over the hazard) so every player sees the crystal from below first
Offer three approaches: walkway kicker, walkway edge rail into the rods, balcony leap from above; one expert approach from below (charged ollie or trampoline)
On a one-way course give a ≈ 15-20 s return route (ramp or speed pad back up) so a miss costs time but not the attempt
Keep the rods' far end and the crystal ≥ ≈ 6.5-7 m above any standable surface, or over water/pit
openQuestions: Heights of the walkway, rods and tape (rough estimates)
Exact VG position of the wrecked car (LP1 8:52 shows a red car beside the walkway)
LP1's path between the tape (8:57), directory 3 (9:08) and A (9:12) suggests a short backtrack; not seen
Which gap bonus the second-balcony route earns (G1 does not name it; probably The Flying Leap)
Whether the remake rods are the original pair plus new lower beams
Course length and scale are low-confidence
